code.text: Short of breath on stairs and on stage for about three months, with a dry cough, tiredness and tightness in the chest; she runs out of breath in the middle of long phrases; twice her heart has raced and she felt faint while singing

She was told after an operation twelve years ago that she had sarcoidosis; no record of that operation is available to this clinic, and she wants a clear answer and a plan that a working singer can keep
Her spring concerts and recording sessions are booked; she does not want to cancel unless she has to, and she needs her voice
No known allergy

code.text: Chest radiograph, two views: bilateral symmetric hilar lymph node enlargement with right paratracheal widening and fine reticulonodular opacities in both upper zones; heart size normal; no effusion

Resting 12-lead ECG: sinus rhythm 84 per minute, PR interval 240 ms (first-degree atrioventricular block), QRS 100 ms, frequent unifocal ventricular ectopic beats; no Q waves; no previous ECG for comparison

High-resolution CT of the chest: symmetric hilar, subcarinal and right paratracheal lymph nodes up to 2.4 cm, some with fine calcification; perilymphatic micronodules along the bronchovascular bundles and fissures in both upper lobes; no fibrosis, traction bronchiectasis or mass

coding.display: Endoscopic endobronchial ultrasonography guided transbronchial needle aspiration of mediastinal lymph node

code.text: Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration of lymph node stations 4R, 7 and 11L under moderate sedation, with bronchoalveolar lavage: non-necrotizing granulomas at all three stations; acid-fast and fungal stains negative; mycobacterial and fungal cultures sent; lavage lymphocytes 32 percent with a CD4 to CD8 ratio of 5.2; no malignant cells
Advance care planning conversation, about 30 minutes, including her wishes about the defibrillator

Full pulmonary function tests (spirometry, lung volumes and diffusing capacity): FVC 74 percent, FEV1 76 percent of predicted, FEV1/FVC 80 percent, total lung capacity 78 percent, DLCO 62 percent of predicted: mild restriction with a reduced diffusing capacity

24-hour Holter monitoring: sinus rhythm 58 to 112 per minute; PR interval 230 to 250 ms throughout; ventricular ectopic beats 6 percent of all beats, unifocal; three runs of nonsustained ventricular tachycardia of up to 8 beats; no second- or third-degree atrioventricular block; palpitations recorded during a run of ectopic beats

Transthoracic echocardiogram: left ventricular ejection fraction 47 percent with thinning and hypokinesis of the basal anteroseptum; normal right ventricle; normal valves; estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 28 mmHg; no pericardial effusion

Cardiac MRI with late gadolinium enhancement: left ventricular ejection fraction 47 percent; patchy mid-wall and subepicardial enhancement of the basal anteroseptum and inferolateral wall (about 9 percent of left ventricular mass), with raised T2 signal in the basal septum; right ventricle normal
Dilated eye examination by ophthalmology: no anterior or posterior uveitis, no conjunctival nodules, intraocular pressure 15 and 16 mmHg, no cataract

Cardiac FDG-PET with perfusion imaging, after 72 hours of a high-fat, very-low-carbohydrate diet and an overnight fast: focal FDG uptake in the basal anteroseptum and lateral wall (maximum SUV 6.2) matching the MRI enhancement, with a mild perfusion defect at the same sites; FDG-avid hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes; no uptake elsewhere outside the chest

Bone density scan (DXA): lumbar spine T-score -1.2, femoral neck T-score -1.6; FRAX adjusted for prednisone of 7.5 mg or more: major osteoporotic fracture 9 percent and hip fracture 1.2 percent at ten years (moderate risk)

coding.display: Cardiac electrophysiologic stimulation and recording study

code.text: Electrophysiology study: HV interval 58 ms; sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (220 per minute) induced with double extrastimuli from the right ventricular apex, ended by overdrive pacing

Implantation of a dual-chamber transvenous cardioverter-defibrillator through the left subclavian vein, programmed with ventricular tachycardia therapies and minimal ventricular pacing; enrolled in remote monitoring; no complications
Repeat spirometry and diffusing capacity after nine weeks of treatment: FVC 84 percent and FEV1 85 percent of predicted, FEV1/FVC 80 percent, DLCO 70 percent of predicted
Repeat cardiac FDG-PET with the same preparation after five months of treatment: no myocardial FDG uptake; perfusion normal; hilar and mediastinal nodes smaller with low uptake
Repeat transthoracic echocardiogram: left ventricular ejection fraction 54 percent; basal septal thinning unchanged; normal right ventricle
Repeat spirometry and diffusing capacity after six months of treatment: FVC 90 percent and FEV1 89 percent of predicted, FEV1/FVC 79 percent, DLCO 76 percent of predicted

description.text: Tissue diagnosis with other causes excluded, and screening of the eyes, heart, calcium, liver and kidneys, within four weeks of presentation

outcomeCode.text: EBUS in nine days; eye examination, Holter, echocardiogram, cardiac MRI and FDG-PET within four weeks

description.text: Calcium in the normal range within three months

outcomeCode.text: Calcium 9.6 mg/dL after nine weeks of treatment

description.text: FVC and DLCO improved by at least 10 percent of predicted within six months

outcomeCode.text: FVC 74 to 90 percent and DLCO 62 to 76 percent of predicted

description.text: No myocardial FDG uptake on repeat PET after about six months of treatment, with left ventricular function stable or better

outcomeCode.text: Myocardial uptake resolved; ejection fraction 54 percent from 47

description.text: Prednisone at 10 mg a day or less by six months, with methotrexate as the steroid-sparing agent

outcomeCode.text: Prednisone 10 mg at six months and tapering

description.text: Back on stage with a schedule she can sustain, with her voice protected

outcomeCode.text: Two concerts a week since late spring; a longer autumn tour planned

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Pulmonology (sarcoidosis) consultation within two weeks, with EBUS-guided lymph node sampling arranged directly from the referral, to confirm the diagnosis and plan treatment
  • Diagnosis of suspected sarcoidosis: chest radiograph and CT of the chest, tissue by EBUS-guided needle aspiration rather than mediastinoscopy, stains and cultures for mycobacteria and fungi, an interferon-gamma release assay and HIV test to exclude other causes; serum ACE is not used to make or exclude the diagnosis
  • Screening every patient with suspected sarcoidosis for other organ involvement: ECG, serum calcium with 25-hydroxyvitamin D and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, creatinine, liver tests and alkaline phosphatase, complete blood count, TSH, and an eye examination; stop the calcium and vitamin D supplement while calcium is high
  • Cardiac evaluation for suspected cardiac sarcoidosis (abnormal ECG and palpitations): 24-hour Holter monitoring, echocardiogram, cardiac MRI with late gadolinium enhancement, and cardiac FDG-PET with a dietary preparation, all before glucocorticoids begin; cardiology and electrophysiology review
  • Treatment of cardiac and pulmonary sarcoidosis: prednisone 40 mg daily, tapered over about six months toward 5 to 10 mg, with methotrexate 15 mg weekly (increased to 20 mg) and folic acid, continued for at least a year for cardiac disease; repeat FDG-PET after about six months
  • Methotrexate safety: hepatitis B and C screening before starting, blood count, liver tests and creatinine every two to four weeks for the first three months and then every eight to twelve weeks, no alcohol, and no trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole while on methotrexate
  • Glucocorticoid protection: bone density scan and FRAX, alendronate weekly, dietary calcium only (no supplements while calcium was high), vitamin D replaced cautiously once calcium is normal, with calcium rechecked; atovaquone pneumocystis prophylaxis while prednisone is 20 mg or more with methotrexate; glucose, blood pressure, weight, mood, sleep and eye pressure checks
  • Vaccination before immunosuppression: PCV20, recombinant zoster vaccine, hepatitis B vaccine for a non-immune adult, influenza and COVID-19 vaccines; no live vaccines while on prednisone and methotrexate
  • Arrhythmia risk: metoprolol for ventricular ectopy; electrophysiology study for a left ventricular ejection fraction above 35 percent with scar on MRI and nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, and a dual-chamber defibrillator if sustained ventricular tachycardia is induced; remote device monitoring, including on tour
  • Performing and travel: concerts paused until the defibrillator wound has healed and the first device check is done, then a lighter schedule with rest days, voice care, and a travel letter with her device card and medicine list; no driving for one week after the implant
  • Depression screening at each phase, plain explanations with written information, and support she chooses; she decides who receives each note

resource.title: Mahalia Jackson synthetic care plan
resource.description: Diagnose and treat sarcoidosis with cardiac involvement in a 52-year-old Black woman and touring singer, in whom sarcoidosis is more common and more often severe and fatal than in White Americans, on the ATS 1958 diagnosis guideline, the ERS 1959 treatment guideline, the HRS 1952 cardiac sarcoidosis consensus and the AHA 1962 scientific statement: chest imaging with bilateral hilar adenopathy; pulmonary function with DLCO; EBUS-guided lymph node aspiration showing non-necrotizing granulomas, with tuberculosis and fungal infection excluded; screening every patient for other organ involvement (eye examination, ECG, calcium and vitamin D handling, liver and kidney tests); cardiac evaluation with ECG, Holter monitoring, echocardiography, cardiac MRI and FDG-PET before treatment begins; prednisone with methotrexate as a steroid-sparing agent, with methotrexate safety monitoring; bone protection that avoids calcium supplements while calcium is high; pneumocystis prophylaxis, vaccination and tuberculosis screening before immunosuppression; arrhythmia risk stratification with electrophysiology study and a defibrillator; and a plan that protects her voice, her performing and her travel.
